unit.title: Clinical Office Practice and Patient Safety

sections.learningObjectives:
- Describe the steps and purpose of exam-room preparation and turnover, including the correct sequence of tasks between patients.
- Maintain exam-room cleanliness and stocking by cleaning and disinfecting surfaces, rotating and replenishing supplies, and disposing of waste correctly.
- Check equipment and uphold patient safety by verifying that equipment functions, identifying hazards, and escalating concerns to licensed staff or supervisors per facility policy.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Think of an exam room like a table at a restaurant. Before a new customer sits down, the table is wiped so the last customer's crumbs and germs do not end up on the next person's plate.

### Question 2

Just like a cook puts on an apron and washes hands before touching dirty dishes, the assistant gets protected before touching anything the last patient used.

### Question 3

Germs are like tiny invisible crumbs. You cannot see them, but they are still there, so you wipe the table every time just in case.

### Question 4

Contact time is like letting soap sit on your hands long enough to do its job. If you wipe the disinfectant away too soon, it has not finished killing the germs.

### Question 5

Cleaning is like sweeping crumbs off a table, and disinfecting is like using a spray that kills the germs you cannot see. You often do both.

### Question 6

The table paper is like a fresh napkin you set out for each guest. Every new patient gets a clean, fresh piece.

### Question 7

Some trash is special, like a broken glass you wrap up separately. Bloody items go in a special red container so no one else touches them.

### Question 8

If your hands have mud on them, you need soap and water, not just hand gel. Blood and dirt are the same idea.

### Question 9

Getting dressed for a messy job is like putting on a raincoat before boots. The gloves go on last so they cover everything else.

### Question 10

When you take off muddy boots, you do it before walking on the clean carpet. Dirty gloves come off first so the germs do not spread.

### Question 11

The paper is like a fresh sheet you put on a bed for a guest. It is clean for each person, but the mattress underneath still gets cleaned too.

### Question 12

A sharps container is like a special box for broken glass. Only sharp, pokey things go in it so nobody gets hurt.

### Question 13

It is like a trash can. When it is full to the line, you take it out and get a new bag so nothing spills over the top.

### Question 14

Dirty laundry is like a dusty blanket. You fold it in gently and drop it in the basket instead of shaking it and making dust fly everywhere.

### Question 15

Even if something looks dry, germs can still be there, so we treat anything with blood on it as a 'handle carefully' item.

### Question 16

It is like setting out all the ingredients before you start cooking, so you do not have to run to the pantry in the middle.

### Question 17

A par level is like the 'low fuel' light in a car. It tells you it is time to refill before you run out.

### Question 18

It is like the milk at the store. The older cartons go in front so people grab them first and nothing goes bad.

### Question 19

It is like a used paper napkin after a meal. If it is not dirty with anything messy, it goes in the normal trash.

### Question 20

A clear path is like a hallway with no toys on the floor, so nobody trips while walking through.

### Question 21

It is like checking that a bathroom has soap and a towel before guests arrive, so everyone can wash their hands.

### Question 22

It is like following a recipe. If you leave out a step or use too much, the result is not what you wanted.

### Question 23

Standard precautions are like wearing a seatbelt on every trip, not just when the road looks dangerous.

### Question 24

Hand gel is great for clean-looking hands, but when your hands are actually dirty, you need soap and water.

### Question 25

High-touch surfaces are like the handle of a classroom door that everyone grabs. Lots of hands touch it, so it gets cleaned a lot.

### Question 26

It is like cleaning up after a meal: clear the dirty dishes, wipe the table, then set out fresh napkins and refill the condiments.

### Question 27

It is like a coach telling the team the game plan. The assistant follows the plan the clinician sets so everyone stays safe.

### Question 28

A blood spill is like a broken glass with sharp edges. You stop, put on protection, and clean it up right away so no one gets hurt.

### Question 29

The doorknob gets touched by everyone, so it gets wiped more often than the top of a bookshelf nobody touches.

### Question 30

You would not use the same dirty sponge to wash dishes and then set the table. Gloves are changed between messy and clean jobs.

### Question 31

A placemat keeps a table clean, but you still wash the table itself. The paper is a helper, not a replacement for cleaning.

### Question 32

It is like a mystery cup in the fridge. You do not drink it or pour it somewhere else; you ask an adult what it is.

### Question 33

A broken toy that does not work gets put in the 'fix it' pile, not handed to a friend. Broken equipment is taken out of use.

### Question 34

It is like checking that a flashlight works before a camping trip. If it is dim, you fix or swap it before you need it.

### Question 35

A used needle is like a pointy stick you put straight into the safe box right away, so nobody gets poked.

### Question 36

If you get a splinter, you wash the spot and tell a grown-up right away. A needlestick is the same idea, only more serious.

### Question 37

Cleaning is like wiping a table for dinner. Sterilizing is like boiling baby bottles so they are completely germ-free. You only need the extra step sometimes.

### Question 38

Moving a big, wobbly box is safer with two people. Helping a patient transfer works the same way, using help when needed.

### Question 39

It is like telling someone you are almost out of milk before the carton is empty, so they buy more in time.

### Question 40

Expired food goes in the 'do not eat' pile. Expired supplies get set aside so nobody uses them by mistake.

### Question 41

It is like a crossing guard who treats every street as busy, even the quiet ones, just to be safe.

### Question 42

Goggles are like wearing safety glasses when something might splash, so it does not get in your eyes.

### Question 43

It is like not eating in the art room where there is paint and glue. You keep food away from messy or harmful things.

### Question 44

Bloody cleanup towels go in the special red bag, just like other things with blood on them.

### Question 45

It is like closing your bedroom door when a guest visits, so they do not see your private things.

### Question 46

It is like a helper setting out the tools for a project while the person in charge does the work.

### Question 47

It is like checking that a chair has all four legs before someone sits in it.

### Question 48

It is like refilling an empty soap pump so everyone can keep washing their hands.

### Question 49

Dirty clothes go straight into the laundry basket, not dropped on the floor where they can spread dirt.

### Question 50

It is like sweeping toward the door instead of back over the clean floor, so the dirt does not spread back.

### Question 51

It is like letting cleaning spray sit on a stain for a minute before you wipe, so it can really work.

### Question 52

A frayed cord is like a wire with its coating worn off. You do not use it; you tell someone to fix it.

### Question 53

It is like replacing an old map with a new one so people get the right directions.

### Question 54

It is like a chore chart with checkmarks, so everyone knows the jobs got done.

### Question 55

After a messy art project, you wipe the whole table, not just the one spot. The assistant cleans everything the wound might have touched.

### Question 56

The sharps box sits right next to where you work, like a small trash can by your desk, so you can toss things in without reaching.

### Question 57

You would not touch clean plates with the same dirty gloves you used to wipe the trash can.

### Question 58

A spilled drink gets wiped up with cleaner, not left to dry sticky on the floor.

### Question 59

It is like using the right kind of cleaner that is proven to work, and following the instructions on the bottle.

### Question 60

It is like making sure the fire extinguisher is in its spot, so it is there in an emergency.

### Question 61

It is like not using the same dirty hands that just touched the trash to answer your phone.

### Question 62

A cracked container of sharp things is like a broken glass jar. You do not touch it with bare hands; you tell an adult.

### Question 63

It is like the fire drill plan: it tells everyone how to stay safe and what to do if something goes wrong.

### Question 64

It is like a cleanup bucket with gloves, rags, and spray all together, so you can clean a mess right away.

### Question 65

When you are not sure which bin something goes in, you ask instead of guessing.

### Question 66

Gloves are like a shield for your hands, keeping icky things off your skin while you work.

### Question 67

It is like the weekly deep clean of the whole house, not just the daily tidying.

### Question 68

If there is a spill that could hurt someone and a tidy-up that can wait, you clean up the dangerous spill first.

### Question 69

Even after taking off dirty gloves, you still wash your hands, just in case anything got through.

### Question 70

It is like letting the oven finish baking even if everyone is hungry. The timing is part of the recipe.

### Question 71

You never try to snap a sharp stick in half with your hands; you put it straight into the safe box.

### Question 72

The color-changing tag is like a seal that proves the job was done. If it did not change, you do not trust the tools.

### Question 73

It is like holding the door and clearing the way for someone carrying something heavy, and telling a grown-up if they need more help.

### Question 74

It is like sorting recycling: sharp things in the sharp box, yucky bloody things in the special bag, and plain paper in the normal bin.

### Question 75

It is like putting on an apron and gloves to do a messy craft, because the instructions say that craft needs them.

### Question 76

It is like knowing which problems you can fix yourself and which ones need an adult in charge.

### Question 77

When the box of pointy things is full, you close it up and get a new box instead of squishing things down.

### Question 78

It is like wiping the table with a cloth you just used on the floor. You just move the dirt around.

### Question 79

It is like reading the instructions before using a new tool, so you do not hurt yourself.

### Question 80

It is like knowing which chores are yours and which ones need a grown-up with special training.

### Question 81

It is like signing your name on a chore chart so everyone knows the job was really done.

### Question 82

It is like using expired medicine that may no longer work when you need it.

### Question 83

It is like putting on gloves before helping with a messy cut, then calling for the grown-up in charge.

### Question 84

Standard precautions are like always washing your hands, and transmission-based precautions are the extra gloves and apron for special jobs.

### Question 85

It is like a deep clean at the end of the week, doing the floors and corners you skip during quick daily tidy-ups.
